items.added_reason: Mean-field theory and the Landau approach are written entirely in the language of free energy minimisation — a quick refresh now means that machinery won't slow you down when you get there.

Scaling laws (Widom, Rushbrooke, Fisher relations) are the quantitative heart of critical phenomena — once you've seen mean-field exponents, deriving the scaling relations shows why universality is nontrivial and motivates the renormalization group.

Linearising RG flow around a fixed point — and reading off relevant vs irrelevant operators from eigenvalues — is pure applied linear algebra and Taylor expansion. A short refresher now keeps the physics front and centre when you hit it.
